approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from a greedy population of accepted high-scoring molecules. Both mutation sources and crossover partners are drawn from preferred score bands, with uniform choice inside each band and exclusion of the first parent when choosing its partner. A fingerprint Gaussian process trained on every accepted label then selects which generated offspring are evaluated. The implementation already favors strong individual parents, but it does not use molecular similarity when deciding which two parents to recombine.
approach.novelty: Condition the crossover partner choice on similarity to the already selected first parent, using the same fingerprint definition that the Parent already declares. More similar eligible partners receive more of the chosen score band's probability, while the first-parent rule and score-band preference remain intact. This tests whether recombining related high-scoring molecules preserves useful local structure more often. The completed siblings altered core balance and survivor diversity; this experiment changes compatibility of a parent pair without replacing survivors or changing crossover chemistry.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-fc2c108a5253 has complete three-replica macro mean 0.5443738005952443 and confirmed posterior-guided graph evolution, but parent pairing is conditioned on score band and distinct identity rather than structural compatibility. A read-only reconstruction of all fifteen Parent task logs and their original accepted serial order finds 1679 accepted crossover offspring, with 172 strict best-parent beats (0.10244192972007148) and mean child-minus-best-parent score -0.15687082230105645; the 2671 mutation offspring give 393 beats (0.1471359041557469) and mean -0.06505340871777952. Crossover has a harder two-parent reference and different selected proposals, so this disparity is not a causal estimate of crossover damage. The molecular review nevertheless documents disrupted useful attachment contexts and repeated large heterocycle assemblies. Completed siblings n-69c038cb49ac and n-28dc36ed5be7 broaden core use but reduce every task mean and weaken realized parent/offspring scores, arguing against assuming that greater structural spread is sufficient. On the Parent's exact post-exclusion partner states, 33542 of 34312 second-parent draws have unequal fingerprint similarities to the first parent. The existing actual mean pair similarity is 0.4830860528997304; uniform selection on the same states has expected mean 0.48383199205456373, while the proposed similarity-proportional law has expected mean 0.5153412733934241. These are existing accepted-molecule comparisons with no alternative descendants or counterfactual oracle scores.
hypothesis: Within the inherited selected score band, sample a crossover partner with probability proportional to its accepted-molecule fingerprint Tanimoto similarity to the already selected first parent.

finding_summary.headline: More similar crossover partners produced more local gains, but lower final scores
finding_summary.insights: The experiment separates selecting related molecules from obtaining more productive chemistry. Similarity enrichment and changed pairings are established, but the smaller parent-relative deficit partly accompanies a weaker reference parent and does not demonstrate stronger absolute offspring. Crossover contributed more local incumbent gains while the inherited mutation stream contributed fewer; mutation is not an unaffected control because new pairings change the accepted population and subsequent random trajectory. Much of the final-score loss came from the second seed's sitagliptin run, so this panel supports negative mean transfer rather than a universal failure of related-parent crossover. Fingerprint relatedness also did not preserve a common core more often: the share of evaluated crossover offspring reusing a generating parent's core fell from 34.25% to 33.00%, while survivor core coverage broadened. The molecular assessment still found repeated large assemblies, reactive halogen connections and strained rings; larger repeated products often offered little score separation from smaller relatives. Thus shared fingerprint features alone did not ensure that the unchanged fragment crossover preserved useful attachment relationships or chemical scale. The conditional-law comparison establishes allocation, but supplies no score for an unchosen partner and no causal attribution for either member of a pair.
finding_summary.results: The intended pairing mechanism changed actual breeding. Of 34,123 partner draws, 33,350 had unequal similarities and used the registered weights; 7,967 choices (23.35%) differed from the passive uniform choice on the same eligible partners and random variate. On nondegenerate states, expected Tanimoto similarity rose from 0.48313 under uniform selection to 0.51979 under the applied law. Actual mean pair similarity rose from the Parent's 0.48309 to 0.51650. The first-parent rule, greedy survival, graph operators and posterior selection remained unchanged. Both runs evaluated 1,679 crossover and 2,671 mutation offspring. Crossover best-parent beats rose from 172 to 176 and sequential incumbent improvements from 75 to 84. Its mean parent-relative deficit narrowed from -0.15687 to -0.13737, but the mean best generating-parent score also fell from 0.43361 to 0.40325, and absolute crossover-offspring score fell from 0.27674 to 0.26587. Raw invalid crossover attempts increased from 123 to 326. Mutation incumbent improvements fell from 143 to 130, leaving fewer total improvements (214 versus 218). The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.54437 to 0.52840, a paired change of -0.01597; seed changes were -0.00054, -0.06139 and +0.01401. All five task means declined, with the largest mean loss on sitagliptin (-0.06334). Every formal task still completed its full evaluation budget.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic carbonyl and amine families carry reactive halogens, strained connections and repeated large assemblies
molecular.overall_character: All current and parent trajectories were read. Each current task has 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The output is predominantly aromatic and ring-bearing: aromatic-token rates range from 0.9701 to 0.9874 and ring-closure rates from 0.9805 to 0.9908. Compact fused heteroaromatic amides, aryl-linked saturated amines and quinoline/pyrrole/lactam combinations coexist with very large repeated dione, ester and carbonate assemblies. The most size-expanded task has mean SMILES length 108.2 and maximum 253, while tiny fragments also occur throughout the trajectories. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. This leaves potentially basic nitrogen centres drawn without a solution ionization state and stereogenic bridged or substituted rings without configurations. Diversity is moderate across seed families but often narrow within a leading series. Familiar medicinal fragments are present, yet overall synthetic plausibility is questionable because N-halogen and acyl-halide groups, N-N and N-O connections, strained small rings, peroxides and reactive unsaturation persist.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are compact fused and bridged aza-aromatic systems with an aryl amide or aryl ketone. Alkyl and ether substitution decorate the ring framework; several leading amides are directly N-fluorinated. A related family contains a conventional N-H amide and a thiophenol substituent, while another has an ordinary sulfur bridge and aryl ketone. Other seeds produce N-chloro amides or cumulated unsaturation in larger heterocycles. The lowest proposals are tiny imine or halogen-containing fragments, and a late elaborated amide product adds another ring/carbonyl connection with a much lower score. Conventional carbonyl fragments are recognizable, but the bridged topology and reactive nitrogen substituents limit synthetic confidence.
liabilities: N-F and N-Cl amides are reactive functionality rather than ordinary aryl halogenation.
Some relatives add thiols, O-Br groups or unusual unsaturation, including a cumulated-double-bond string rate of 0.0816.
Bridged ring arrangements and appended carbonyl rings increase geometric and synthetic complexity.
missing_features: The lowest fragments and over-elaborated products lose the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement retained by the stronger molecules.

Matched stable nitrogen substituents and ordinary ring connections around the leading framework are incomplete; the N-H amide and conventional sulfide/ketone relatives already show viable alternative chemistry.
Configurations at substituted bridge atoms are unspecified, and cumulated unsaturation in other relatives lacks a demonstrated feasible geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methyl-substituted fused N-fluoroamide scores 0.44941366017785356 with either para aryl bromine or chlorine. Replacing a ring methyl by methylthio gives 0.4166419114047398 for the same halogen pair, so sulfur addition is not rewarded in that local comparison. A conventional N-H amide relative reaches 0.4254027310763201 and an aryl ketone/sulfide relative reaches 0.42570769607214154; N-fluorination is therefore not universal among the stronger outputs. The more elaborated final amide structure scores 0.015332630870835013, and tiny fragments score 0.0. Current seed 2 reaches 0.44941366017785356 versus parental 0.4163503402962837 with a different N-fluoro carbonyl framework. Current seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.4163503402962837 and 0.40143692941489145 versus parental 0.4463521672202675 and 0.4126819838532174. These observations favor a compact aromatic carbonyl arrangement without isolating one universally required heteroatom bond.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family contains N-methylated heteroaromatic diones, substituted aza-aromatic ester groups and imine-containing unsaturated side chains with oxygen-linked alkynes. Some members join multiple copies of these motifs through branched carbon or ether-containing connections. Additional variants contain a chlorinated oxime ether connection, cyanate-like substitution or direct N-chlorination. Seed 0 produces very large multiaryl ester/carbonate assemblies with several nitriles; seed 1 develops fused carbonyl-rich heterocycles. The low tail includes simple hydrocarbons and an extremely strained small cyclic alkyne. The output has abundant polar and aromatic fragments, but repeated growth and reactive appendages dominate practical synthesis concerns.
liabilities: Oxygen-linked alkynes, imines, chlorinated oxime ethers, direct N-Cl and O-Cl variants introduce reactive chemistry.
Repeated dione/aryl/ester units and many ester or carbonate connections add size, flexibility and hydrolysis-sensitive bonds.
The small cyclic alkyne in the low tail is a particularly clear example of graph validity not establishing a plausible molecular geometry.
missing_features: Small isolated fragments lack the connected aromatic and carbonyl arrangement of the stronger products.
The leading set incompletely represents stable, less repetitive structures that retain the useful core; the smaller example already has a score close to much larger relatives.
Imine/alkene geometry and configurations of branched linkers are unassigned, while some small-ring alternatives require extreme geometric distortion.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading decorated dione/ester structure scores 0.6071971741156846. A substantially smaller member retaining a single dione/aza-aromatic core reaches 0.6060752169720347; extending an alkyl substituent or replacing N-methyl by N-chloro preserves exactly that score. Larger linked variants reach 0.606951871657754 or 0.6065327120947389, offering little separation from the smaller framework. Multiaryl ester/carbonate variants both score 0.6061163101604278 despite a change in peripheral nitrile substitution. Tiny or isolated reactive fragments score 0.5. The molecular evidence favors retention of the organized aromatic/carbonyl framework but does not show a strong need for its repeated appendages. Current per-seed maxima are 0.6061163101604278, 0.6025580572910527 and 0.6071971741156846, versus parental 0.6004556752278376, 0.6324703199409752 and 0.6083454583246726.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules combine diarylmethyl aromatic groups with primary aryl amino and N-fluoroamino substituents, an available saturated-ring amine and a fluoroethyl-substituted pyrrolidine. Linker and ring topology vary between relatively open amine chains, small nitrogen rings and spiro or bridged arrangements. A similarly strong seed-0 family instead has chlorinated anisyl groups, a carbinolamine-like connection and a constrained bicyclic saturated amine, without direct N-F. Other seed-1 products contain unusually coordinated sulfur. The low examples are acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives or isolated halogenated carbonyl/alcohol fragments. Recognizable aryl-amine chemistry is present, but N-halogen groups, unstable connection types and undefined configurations remain common.
liabilities: Direct N-F groups and alpha-haloamine or carbinolamine-like connections can be reactive or chemically labile.
Small nitrogen rings, cyclopropane-fused saturated amines and spiro systems create strain and configurational complexity.
More elaborate relatives combine multiple basic centres and hydrophobic aromatic groups, and occasional unusual sulfur bonding persists in another seed.
missing_features: The low acid/amide/sulfonamide and small fragment products lack the integrated aromatic and accessible aliphatic-amine arrangement found in stronger molecules.
Stable matched replacements for N-fluoroamino and carbinolamine-like connections are incomplete, although different high-scoring families show that no single reactive connection is universal.
Stereochemistry at substituted saturated rings and bridge atoms is absent; the scores do not establish a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-fluoroaryl/diarylmethyl/saturated-amine leader scores 0.9862523132425369. The seed-0 carbinolamine/bicyclic-amine compound reaches 0.9860539690682922 and a less constrained amine-chain relative scores 0.9829644103093601. Thus strong observed scores occur across distinct aryl/amine frameworks and do not establish a need for direct N-F or maximal ring constraint. A related open amine chain in seed 2 reaches 0.9790824394553618. An expanded, partly dearomatized version of the substituted aryl group scores 0.18447496826975118, while the low acid/amide/sulfonamide example scores 0.0005876222816323224. A small anisyl alcohol/chloromethyl fragment scores 0.0015965585288304303. These observations support the combined aromatic/aliphatic-amine arrangement rather than either fragment alone. Current seed maxima are 0.9860539690682922, 0.9538130524845956 and 0.9862523132425369, versus parental 0.9908331648929692, 0.9512348232667347 and 0.9914038363125457.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family combines an alkylquinoline ether, a pyrrole ring and a nitrogen-rich cyclic carbonyl framework. The latter varies between expanded lactam/hydrazine-like rings, fused carbonyl heterocycles and N-O-containing connections. Alkylamino and acetyl substituents recur. Other seeds produce larger fused ester/carbamate structures or peroxide-containing cyclic diones. The very low examples are small molecules such as methane, water, acetylene and hydroxymethyl fragments that lack the leading framework. The principal fragments are recognizable, but N-N and N-O bonds, peroxide alternatives and expanded fused rings make the assembled structures less conventional.
liabilities: N-N, N-O and peroxide connections introduce chemical lability in otherwise recognizable carbonyl-ring families.
Additional ring fusions and expanded heterocycles add synthetic and conformational complexity without a clear local score advantage.
Repeated structures and tiny fragments still appear alongside the useful aromatic/carbonyl organization.
missing_features: The lowest fragments lack the integrated aromatic and carbonyl-containing nitrogen framework of the stronger molecules.

The displayed series incompletely covers ordinary stable carbon/nitrogen ring connections preserving the same fragment placement; closely scoring variants do not establish a need for N-O or hydrazine-like bonds.
Expanded ring conformations and stereogenic alternative frameworks remain undefined, and no single unseen functional group is established as the missing objective feature.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The quinoline-ether/pyrrole/cyclic nitrogen-carbonyl leader scores 0.21843931889797025, while a related acetyl/carbonyl framework reaches 0.21821789023599233. Several nitrogen-, oxygen- or carbon-linked variants remain close: 0.21505649253221687, 0.21387513707167027 and 0.2133697489012744. A methylene insertion into the aryl-ether connection gives 0.2120637831740049. These comparisons support the overall quinoline/pyrrole/carbonyl organization more clearly than a unique N-N or N-O connection. Tiny fragments score 0.0, and additional fused-ring elaboration in final molecules remains around 0.2000100007500625 to 0.2030079876549599. Current seed 2 reaches 0.21843931889797025 versus parental 0.21037674112349405 with a different quinoline-linked expanded dicarbonyl framework. Current seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.2088465157016203 and 0.2118805753879094 versus parental 0.22405709718343647 and 0.2133697489012744.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest family combines a nitrogen-containing fused dione bearing direct N-F substituents, a small unsaturated carbon ring and a methylamino-substituted cyclopentadiene-like ring carrying an acyl fluoride. Free thiol or sulfur-linked ring closures occur in relatives. A second family has a more fused carbonyl-rich aza framework with carbon-bound fluorine and an aryl acyl fluoride, while another seed produces aldehyde-bearing sulfur/nitrogen heterocycles. These are moderate-sized but chemically reactive structures. The low tail is dominated by large coupled dione units or highly elaborated sugar/aryl assemblies, including examples that already carry acyl fluorides.
liabilities: Acyl fluoride and direct N-F are reactive bonds and should not be conflated with ordinary stable carbon fluorination.
Small unsaturated rings, free thiols, sulfur-linked cages and aldehydes add stability or strain concerns.
Large coupled diones and complex sugar/aryl assemblies create severe size and topology deviations from the stronger molecules.
missing_features: The low repeated assemblies lack the useful compact arrangement despite carrying some of the same dione or fluorinated groups.

The displayed leaders lack a matched series retaining the carbonyl and fluorinated-group geometry while replacing acyl fluoride and direct N-F with stable alternatives. Their presence in stronger molecules does not establish chemical necessity.
The stronger parental aminomethyl/fluorinated-aryl dione arrangement is not recovered among the current leading families.
Configurations of substituted small rings and unsaturated-ring geometries remain unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading acyl-fluoride/N-fluorinated dione scores 0.5176146979065886. Adding fluorine to its small carbon ring gives 0.5099566511392558, while chlorine there gives 0.4470674757352588. A more bridged sulfur-containing relative scores 0.4780400812140165, so additional ring closure does not improve that comparison. The second fused family reaches 0.44237693944672385 with fluoromethyl substitution, and related carbon-bound fluorine arrangements score 0.4337016156471047 or 0.4333617268342616. These observations associate stronger scores with a compact carbonyl-rich framework and specific fluorinated-group placement, not maximal fluorine count. Large repeated dione assemblies score as low as 1.7287338239402662e-48; some contain acyl fluoride too, showing that this group alone is insufficient. Current seed 0 and seed 2 reach 0.5176146979065886 and 0.44237693944672385 versus parental 0.4759777345546235 and 0.4071395189354175. Current seed 1 reaches 0.3176770239241658 versus parental 0.5845583988949146 with a more conventional aminomethyl/fluorinated-aryl dione family.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited output includes N-F and N-Cl groups, acyl fluorides, N-O and N-N connections, peroxides and oxygen-linked alkynes. Strong alternatives with conventional N-H amide or sulfide/ketone connections reach 0.4254027310763201 and 0.42570769607214154, and distinct aryl/amine families reach similar scores with different reactive groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive bond types remain entangled with useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide matched stable substitutions that preserve useful fragment placement. Distinguish ordinary amides, amines, thioethers and carbon-bound halogens from acyl-halide, heteroatom-halogen and other labile connections.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The most size-expanded proposal set has mean SMILES length 108.2 and maximum 253. A smaller dione/aza-aromatic member scores 0.6060752169720347, close to much larger relatives at 0.606951871657754, while tiny fragments sit at low baselines and large repeated dione assemblies can score 1.7287338239402662e-48.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still produces excessive repetition and tiny fragments instead of consistently preserving useful molecular scale.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand chemical variety through coherent changes in scaffold, substitution and linker geometry while preserving the useful core size. Include simplifications that remove whole repeated units or unnecessary appendages without destroying the principal functional-group arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The cited molecules contain substituted bridges, small nitrogen rings, cyclopropane-fused amines, unsaturated small carbon rings and an extremely strained small cyclic alkyne. Other structures add expanded rings and imine geometry that cannot be judged from aromatic or closure tokens alone.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring geometry and stereochemical identity remain unresolved for constrained or unsaturated products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer ordinary ring topologies and feasible configurations, preserve stereochemical assignments when structures change, and compare matched alternatives with different constraints. Successful parsing should not substitute for chemically plausible geometry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Aryl bromine and chlorine relatives share 0.44941366017785356, while replacing a methylthio substituent by methyl raises the displayed pair to that value from 0.4166419114047398. Several alkyl or N-chloro substitutions leave another family at 0.6060752169720347, and multiple carbon/nitrogen/oxygen connection variants retain closely similar scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Matched local simplifications are incomplete where additional complexity has little demonstrated score value.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate matched changes that remove unnecessary substitution, unstable bonds or extra ring connections while holding the useful aromatic and polar fragments fixed. Let observed feedback distinguish necessary geometry from tolerated embellishment.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
